newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Hyundai unveils new MPV in Geneva.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai unveils new MPV in Geneva.

text.p: South Korean car maker Hyundai Motor on Tuesday unveiled its new H-1 Multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), which it plans to sell in all the main world markets.
The H-1, which cost $185 million to develop, can seat up to 12 in a long-wheelbase version, Hyundai executive managing director S.I. Lee said.

Lee, in a speech at the Geneva car show, declined to price the vehicle, which in short-wheelbase form will compete in the MPV sector which includes models like the Renault Espace, Volkswagen Sharan and Ford Galaxy.
"We haven't decided on the price yet, but it will certainly be competitive," Lee said.
The H-1 will go on sale in Europe in September and will probably appear in north American markets in the 1999 model year, Lee said.

The arrival of another MPV -- a luxury van usually seating up to eight -- is bad news for the European manufacturers. They have all invested heavily in MPVs, only to find sales failing to come up to expectations.
Some production lines have been forced to switch to commercial van production.
Questioned after his speech, Lee said Hyundai hoped to sell 11,000 H-1s annually in Europe.
European H-1 customers can choose a 2.4 litre petrol engine, or a 2.5 litre turbocharged diesel.
